description: Reference properties for viscoelastic, glassy and granular slide materials. Each record describes one specimen or formulation.

conventions.null: A relevant property has no calibrated value for this specimen in the cited source. A numeric consumer must explicitly handle this case.
conventions.missing: This record supplies no default for the property. Absence and null both differ from a measured zero.
conventions.range: Endpoints describe the stated range only. They do not define a sampling distribution.
conventions.models: Flow and optics model names are intended simulation treatments. Measurements belong to their named specimen and experimental scale.

materials.name: Slime · aqueous PVA–borate gel
materials.specimen: B3, prepared from separate aqueous solutions of GM14 poly(vinyl alcohol) and sodium borate.

flow.interpretation: Approximate peak of the linear relaxation spectrum, from an eleven-mode fit across the series including B3. A one-mode approximation retains this characteristic time. The source observed age-dependent nonlinear response.

materials.name: Hard candy · cast sugar optic
materials.specimen: Uncolored hard candy optic made from table sugar, light corn syrup and distilled water. Cooled solid.

flow.applicableState: Cast and cured at the end of cooling, before moisture uptake or reheating.

optics.refractiveIndexQualifier: Approximate bulk index reported by the inventor. The patent defines approximate values to within 5%.
optics.appearance: Transparent with a slight golden tint.

materials.name: Hard sugar glass · melt-quenched sucrose
materials.specimen: Crystalline sucrose heated in a DSC pan and immediately cooled to produce the glass. Heating can discolor sucrose.

flow.applicableState: Dry glass on performance timescales well below the measured transition.
flow.glassTransitionMethod: Midpoint on the second DSC scan at 10 °C/min.

optics.appearance: The authors observed transparent yellow material after the second DSC scan.

materials.name: Magic Sand · submerged coated grains
materials.specimen: Commercial Magic Sand used by Karmakar and colleagues. Polyhedral grains with hydrophobic surface patches, immersed with trapped air.

flow.skinInterfacialEnergyQualifier: Approximate measured effective energy of the aggregate skin.
flow.contactAngleMethod: Approximate angles for a water drop on a single grain. Advancing and receding values were obtained by tilting.

optics.applicableState: The air-retaining skin gives the submerged aggregate its luster. Degassing removes the observed luster.

materials.name: Hydrophobic sand · paraffin-coated silica
materials.specimen: Laboratory silica sand bearing a nanoscale paraffin coating.

flow.contactAngleMethod: Approximate values. Condensed water microdroplets on individual grains, and added or withdrawn water on a packed bed for the two macroscopic angles.
